description: We are ASTRAEON, a team of students passionate about space exploration, astronomy, science, and technology. Our project brings NASA’s spacecraft and missions to life through interactive exploration, storytelling, and scientific information. We welcome creative and enthusiastic participants skilled or interested in web development, UI/UX design, 3D modelling, astronomy research, content writing, and problem-solving. Join us to explore the universe through innovation!

details:
ASTRAEON – The Stories of Spacecraft Beyond Their Missions

ASTRAEON is an interactive space exploration website developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, addressing the challenge “Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA’s Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars.” The project aims to bring the stories of spacecraft, landers, rovers, and scientific equipment left behind during space exploration to life.

What Does the Project Do and How Does It Work?

ASTRAEON transforms space exploration into an engaging and interactive learning experience. Users can explore a space-themed environment, navigate between celestial bodies, and discover spacecraft and equipment associated with past NASA missions. The website integrates mission information, scientific discoveries, historical timelines, and spacecraft locations into its exploration experience.

Through interactive exploration, users can learn about objects such as the Apollo Lunar Modules, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Viking landers, and other spacecraft. The website also incorporates spacecraft storytelling, where missions narrate their experiences through creative educational dialogue clearly distinguished from authentic NASA transmissions. Mission timelines and scientific information help users understand the purpose, achievements, and eventual fate of these spacecraft.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ASTRAEON makes complex space science more accessible and enjoyable, particularly for students and young space enthusiasts. It encourages curiosity, independent learning, and interest in astronomy, planetary science, and space technology.

The project highlights the scientific and historical value of spacecraft that are no longer operational, showing that even after their missions end, they continue to contribute to humanity’s understanding of the universe. ASTRAEON hopes to inspire future scientists, engineers, and explorers while preserving the stories of humanity’s achievements in space.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software

The project is developed as a web-based interactive experience using:

  • HTML – for the structure and content of the website.
  • CSS – for the visual design, layout, animations, and responsiveness.
  • JavaScript – for interactive exploration, navigation, controls, and dynamic features.
  • NASA’s publicly available mission information and scientific resources – for accurate mission details and educational content.
  • GitHub – for source-code management and project hosting.
  • Claude AI – for assistance with coding, refining website features, and development.
  • Gamma AI – for assistance in preparing the project presentation.

The project primarily uses software and web technologies and does not require specialized hardware.

Creativity and Innovation

ASTRAEON combines scientific education with interactive exploration and storytelling. Instead of presenting spacecraft information as a conventional list or article, it allows users to discover mission stories through an immersive space environment.

Its creative features include interactive exploration, spacecraft-inspired narration, mission timelines, and the integration of scientific facts with engaging storytelling. This approach transforms abandoned or retired space equipment into meaningful educational experiences and gives users a new perspective on space exploration.

Factors Considered by the Team

During development, the team considered scientific accuracy, educational value, accessibility, user experience, and technical feasibility. NASA mission information and official resources were considered important for ensuring that the content remains reliable.

The team also focused on making the website understandable for school-age audiences, maintaining a clear and user-friendly interface, and preserving the distinction between factual scientific information and creative storytelling. The project was designed to be accessible through a web browser and suitable for further development and expansion.

ASTRAEON ultimately aims to demonstrate that the end of a spacecraft’s mission does not mean the end of its story. Every piece of equipment left in space represents a milestone in humanity’s journey of discovery.
